newsitem.title: UK: UK Oct house prices up 0.8 pct - Nationwide.
newsitem.headline: UK Oct house prices up 0.8 pct - Nationwide.

text.p: released the following UK house price data -
HOUSE PRICES (index base Q1 1993 ) OCT SEPT OCT'95
Nationwide's marketing and commercial director Peter Williamson said this year's trend of rising house prices was at last being complemented by a stronger trend in house sales.
"Even so, the weakness of the market at the beginning of this year is illustrated by the fact that in 1996 transactions will probably underperform 1994," he said.

"There is evidence to suggest that numbers of both first time and subsequent buyers are increasing. However, localised pressure on prices, created by supply shortages, continue to affect middle sectors of the market, particularly in the south."
"We expect such pressures to diminish as improvements in homeowners' equity encourage more property onto the market and facilitate trading up," Williamson said.
House prices were still about a third below their peak in real terms and improvements in the market were far from uniform.
"The recovery, therefore, has much further to go, although a return to previous peaks in activity is not anticipated," he said.
